# ODD

Tier 3. The Outcome-Driven Development profile: graph-native product
authoring over a declared asset graph. It imports the families that
[§1 Foundation to law](#foundation-to-law) lists by reference under
[PROFILES §1](PROFILES.md#1-the-boundary) and restates none of them. Inside
its bounded context it uses its own terms freely: graph, node, asset,
vector, edge, graph function, traversal, worksite, ledger, event log, GTL,
ABG, F_P and F_H (P0, P1). `F_D` is the exact-edition common import below.

Two definitions are used here and owned elsewhere. The a_c traversal record
and the functor kinds are
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds);
the core result algebra is [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results).
This profile's graph traversal and its F_P and F_H shorthands are its
own concepts and are not those records by spelling. Its F_D use imports
the common kind through [§5](#probabilistic-compute), without inheriting
any operation authority. The Executive, Worker
and Reviewer of [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md) are roles, and roles
are relations over steps in which no role name confers an operation
([ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)); the actor, the
executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are different
coordinates (AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5) (P3, P6).

heading: ODD/2. Method role
text:
## 2. Method role

[SPEC_METHOD](SPEC_METHOD.md) is the general constitutional method: the
baseline for goals, intent, product, requirements, design and lawful
re-entry. This profile is the graph-native ODD product-authoring method
whose primary constructive carrier is GTL-defined graph functions. It holds
two kinds of law: constitutional law for graph-native traversal governance
(assets, vectors, traversal, graph functions), and product-authoring law
for building an ODD product correctly over that substrate (P1, P6).

The profile does not replace a product-specific domain method such as the
world-model profile (WORLD_MODEL, tier 3). Where a product is both ODD and
world-model-driven, this profile governs graph-native structure and ODD
product shape and the world-model profile governs world-model semantics,
publication and composition law. The two compose (P1, P4a).

heading: ODD/3. Method composition
text:
## 3. Method composition

This profile alone does not suffice for domain-correct product work. It
gives the structural law for how a graph-native ODD product should be
built. It does not give the product's domain semantics, its current intent
and product-definition line, its local capability and constraint
requirements, or its currently ratified design surfaces (P1, P2).

The composition rule: this profile says how to build the product as a
graph-native ODD product; domain methods say what semantic law the product
must honour; the local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, requirements and design say
what the currently ratified local line is. For a graph-native
software-development ODD product, this profile provides the substrate and
structural law and the product's local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`,
requirements, design records and GTL surfaces provide the local line. For
a world-model product, this profile provides the substrate and structural
law, the world-model profile provides the semantic law, and the product's
local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, requirements and design provide the local
line (P1, P2).

An agent that reads only this profile should understand the paradigm.
To build one concrete product correctly it must then read the
product-specific method and the local authority surfaces (P1, P2).

heading: ODD/11. Core law
text:
## 11. Core law

An ODD product is built correctly only when every clause of this section
holds (P6).

heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.7A Conforming agentic development
text:
### 11.7A Conforming agentic development

This profile is the premise for conforming agentic development over the
graph-native worksite. An agentic coder produces governed work by
following the constitutional process over a minimal declared authority
packet, and admission gates the artifacts it produces. SPEC_METHOD governs
the general constitutional process and [TICKETS](TICKETS.md) governs
artifact admission; this section names the ODD specialisation and composes
that law without declaring it again (P6, P0).

Conformance has two halves: an F_P walkthrough supplying evidence that the
process can be followed, and a declared admission gate assessing the produced
artifacts under its evidence contract and grant. A gate claiming F_D also
establishes the common kind's eligibility under §5; its kind is no authority
to admit (P6).

The walkthrough is the conformance proof. §11.7 requires automation to
stay true for a manual walkthrough; its agentic form is a conformance test
of the method itself. An agentic coder executes the constitutional process
end to end on real work, using only the declared authority surfaces:
intake triage, the smallest lawful re-entry, the specification,
requirement, design and ticket chain, the constructive evaluation loop of
§11.5D, and closure proof. The agentic coder is F_P over the
constitutional process (P0, P6).

The agent works from a minimal declared authority packet, not from memory
and not from wholesale hidden context. The general method already requires
declared context for any agentic work unit: input and output contract,
required context, role, evaluator regime and provenance (SPEC_METHOD;
[ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#1-the-step)). The ODD addition is that the
packet carries only the smallest declared authority sufficient to decide
the step, with its source refs, and that conformance is enforced by
admitting the produced artifact rather than by enlarging what the agent
must hold. Compression is prompt input and never the deciding authority
(P0, P6). What a derived surface may decide is owned by
[ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),
Acquisition and Standalone scope; this section adds only the ODD limit
that follows. A derived surface or projected frame of the general method may
orient the agent to source precedence, lawful re-entry and traceability;
it must not be used to decide product-specific behaviour, which must come
from the current product authority packet (P6, P1).

The walkthrough proves at two levels. The work it produces must be lawful:
correct change class, traceable, admitted. A point where the walkthrough
cannot proceed is a method defect only when a competent agent, correctly
configured and using the declared authority, still cannot decide because
of ambiguity, a missing step, contradictory authority or an undecidable
change class in an owning surface. That defect is repriced into the owning
authority surface, as a failed manual traversal is a graph defect under
§11.7 (P6, P5).

An agent that ignored the declared authority, relied on stale memory or
reasoned badly has produced agent error, not a method defect. Admission
rejects the malformed artifact either way, so a bad agent turn neither
becomes law nor silently indicts the method (P6).

This proof is independent of any automated runtime. A live lane that
depends on external execution conditions, such as an overloaded model API
or a flaky transport, cannot prove the constitutional process sound,
because it conflates process validity with runtime availability. The
walkthrough proves the process; the runtime only executes it (P6, P5).

The validator is the conformance gate. The constitutional process is an
interface contract, and interface conformance is enforced by validating
artifacts against the contract, not by the conformer holding the contract.
This profile does not declare the artifact rules again: tickets,
change-class declarations, design-module derivations and execution
contracts are admitted under SPEC_METHOD and TICKETS, which already require
a drafted classification to be admitted or rejected against deterministic
criteria rather than taken as automatic truth. This profile requires only
that agentic development pass through that admission. The agentic coder
produces the artifact; the declared admission gates it deterministically,
fail-closed and naming the violated rule, exactly as a typed asset is
enforced by its constructor (§11.1) (P6, P3).

This keeps the F_P and F_D split at the method layer. The agentic coder is
F_P: it reasons, drafts and proposes within the declared packet. Admission
uses F_D only when the §5 total-domain contract is established, and its own
contract and authority determine what artifact-conformance decision it may
make. An unresolved eligibility assessment stays open under the migration
relation; an unchanged-subject evaluator still preserves that subject. The walkthrough
establishes that the process can be followed; admission establishes that
each act of following it conforms (P6, P0).

Conformance is not approval by usage. A passed admission and a completed
walkthrough are conformance evidence, not ratification. Shared method
change still follows §9: repeated agentic execution does not make grey
work constitutional. The agentic coder conforms to the method; it does not
amend the method by acting (P6).

heading: ODD/15. Release boundary
text:
## 15. Release boundary

A release version is not constitutional graph truth; it belongs to the
release process and release metadata. The graph-native method concerns
current assets, current vectors, current closures and current authority.
Immutable publication, applicable RC selector advancement and exact-cut
acceptance stay a separate process surface, [RELEASE](RELEASE.md) (P3,
P6).

heading: ODD/16. Failure pattern
ODD/19. Ramp-up checklist
text:
## 19. Ramp-up checklist

An LLM ramping into an ODD product should quickly answer (P0, P2):

1. What is the product's semantic chain from source to published outcome?
2. What are the typed domain assets or nodes?
3. What are the public graph functions?
4. Where is the machine-readable function catalogue?
5. Where is the GTL module?
6. What belongs to ABG and what to the product?
7. What is the projection and query lane?
8. Which admitted carrier, runtime, event or source truth does each
   projection derive from, and how does it fail closed on structural
   drift?
9. What proves that execution authority has not escaped ABG into product
   or plugin code?
10. What is the product's constructive evaluation loop from observation to
    the next lawful action?
11. What are the closure decision dispositions, and how is `yield`
    represented as replay-visible lawful iteration?
12. Which proof surfaces close the current capabilities?
13. Which outer carrier stays open if a refined inner lane is green but
    live requirements still lack executable proof?
14. Can an agentic coder follow the constitutional process from the
    declared authority alone, and do the artifacts it produces pass
    deterministic admission?

If those questions cannot be answered quickly, the product is not yet
sufficiently ODD-shaped (P0, P2).

heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition/Product composition contract
text:
### Product composition contract

The following clauses apply the shared authority, identity, context,
preservation and change laws to Product composition. They define no second
admission or result algebra. A Product may consume, coordinate or assess
another Product through its declared relation; these roles are neither a closed
nor disjoint kind taxonomy, and none confers authority (P6, P3).

[The contract template](templates/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION_CONTRACT_TEMPLATE.md)
projects these coordinates; [the recursive example](examples/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION.md)
works them through a shared leaf and an independently enterable composite.
[CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md#product-composition-discriminators) names their
positive and adverse discriminators. These artifacts apply this owner (P1, P6).

heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition/PC-01 — Recursive Product boundaries
text:
### PC-01 — Recursive Product boundaries

A Product identifies one coherent WHAT and its owning authority. Alternative
realizations of that WHAT are build tenants. A decomposition into Products names
which distinct outcomes and authorities each constituent owns, and which outer
outcome the composition owns.

Under the identity and ownership laws (P3, P6), within a declared decomposition scope, a leaf has no further constituent Product
boundary exposed by that decomposition. It may contain modules and declared
external dependencies. A composite relates two or more constituent capabilities
or an outer capability to its constituent capability; its own capability may in
turn be consumed as a constituent. The same definition, contract and authority
laws apply at every depth. Shared constituents keep one identity and their
separately bound uses; a hierarchy view may show several references to one leaf.

Decomposition, capability/data dependency, inspection permission, authority and
work prerequisites are distinct relations. A directory tree establishes none of
them. A named composition view states its root, participating identities,
selected boundaries and relation kinds rather than treating all reachable edges
as one hierarchy.

heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition/PC-02 — Independent entry and the integrated outcome
text:
### PC-02 — Independent entry and the integrated outcome

A Product offered as a standalone constituent must be enterable through its own
Product Definition and a Product-authorized applicable frame basis, with the
dependency closure and capabilities its contract declares. Entry must not require
an enclosing composition's activation unless that enclosing capability is itself
an explicit prerequisite. Such a prerequisite is disclosed as a limit on the
standalone claim. Shared or externally located frame documents are permitted
where adoption, scope and availability are established; file ownership alone is
not the deciding test.

Standalone does not imply dependency-free, separately deployable or able to
supply every host itself. The claim names which construction, evaluation or use
can be performed independently and its required inputs. The composition owner
separately establishes interface compatibility, material joins and its complete
outcome. Successful constituent checks do not establish that outer predicate.

heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition/PC-03 — The edge's contract and authority record
text:
### PC-03 — The edge's contract and authority record

For each directed relation, the `relation` authority and referenced `contracts`
state, directly or by exact reference:

1. Source and target Product identities and roles; the consumed capability,
   outcome, purpose, selected basis and currentness policy.
2. The existing owners and grants for each material operation: acquisition,
   disclosure, use, execution, mutation, assessment and disposition. A kind or
   role label records no grant by itself.
3. Admissible inputs and exports; material assumptions, effects, failures,
   obligations and evidence; restrictions on implementation material and derived
   information where applicable.
4. The acting principals or binding rule, task/phase scope, permitted delegation,
   return consumer, stop/refusal conditions and revocation/invalidation route.

These coordinates may be supplied by source-linked prose. The relation locates
and constrains lawfully granted authority; it cannot manufacture the target's
permission or the source's admission. Missing material authority or an unresolved
conflict withholds the dependent action. The execution-scoped activation remains
the place where a particular actor, input, effect and return are bound.

heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition/PC-04 — Recursive authority and information eligibility
text:
### PC-04 — Recursive authority and information eligibility

A permitted A → B use does not entail A's access to B's dependencies. Neither
A → B plus B → C nor two routes to a shared leaf imply a union of their grants.
Each onward acquisition, disclosure or delegated effect needs authority for that
actor, purpose and path, including any permitted onward use of returned material.
Existing delegation may authorize a chain explicitly; its scope cannot expand
silently at a recursive step.

A provider may encapsulate internal dependencies behind an adequate contract.
Consumers need not flatten every implementation dependency into a direct edge.
Where an outer claim materially relies on a far-side contract, assumption,
evidence item or acquisition, that reliance and its applicable authority must be
preserved through the boundary. Unknown impact is not evidence of encapsulation.

Durable Product consumption and bounded authorized inspection are different
relations. A Reviewer or diagnostic Worker may inspect a larger causal cone under
an explicit access grant without thereby adopting those internals as a runtime
dependency or gaining a write grant. If findings become a continuing construction
constraint or dependency, their producer, applicability and governing relation
must be retained.

heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition/PC-05 — Context construction and clean-room conditions
text:
### PC-05 — Context construction and clean-room conditions

An actor's selected context must satisfy both permission and adequacy for its
engagement. Permission covers the source information and permitted derivations,
not only paths or filenames. The boundary identifies eligible source classes,
exports and tool outputs, material provenance, intended use, later acquisitions
and the effect of prior exposure. An allowed file location or a fresh summary
does not sanitize prohibited information.

A target owner may authorize an export, but clean-room eligibility additionally
requires that the engagement's information policy admits that export and its
provenance. The actual delivered/acquired material must be recorded to the extent
required by the claim. An uncertain or prohibited exposure follows the declared
hold/re-entry rule; it cannot be repaired by deleting its receipt or relabeling
the same actor fresh. Prior actor knowledge and external acquisition channels are
part of the declared limits.

Adequacy retains the distinctions required for the task's decisions and
continuations, including unresolved obligations, result standing, currentness and
authority. If the permitted material is insufficient, acquire an authorized
extension, narrow the task with the owner, use a suitable actor or return the
unresolved outcome. Permission is not evidence of sufficiency, and a budget is
not permission to omit a deciding condition. This applies [FOUNDATIONS Observation sufficiency](FOUNDATIONS.md#assurance-relations)
and its scoped preservation law; it supplies no general optimal context selector (P1, P2, P6).

heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition/PC-06 — Readiness, cycles and replacement
text:
### PC-06 — Readiness, cycles and replacement

Work selects a dependency-ready frontier at the required subjects and revisions.
A cycle in declared Product relationships need not be a cycle in the selected
work. A cycle of current prerequisite claims requires an executable resolution:
for example an admitted prior revision, explicit seed, staged contract or bounded
iteration with its continuation/stop conditions. Naming a lead alone does not
supply a missing prerequisite or establish convergence.

Replacing a constituent or refining it into further Products preserves the
consumer's material contract: meaning, preconditions, effects, failures,
authority, lifecycle, evidence and subsequent obligations. A semantic change
requires an authorized successor relation and affected reassessment. The [ACTIVATION refinement contract](ACTIVATION.md#refinement) governs this
preservation. Matching signatures, labels or a sample output is insufficient (P4a, P6). New capabilities may be
added without silently widening existing consumers' duties or grants.

heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition/PC-07 — Change, evidence and reliance
text:
### PC-07 — Change, evidence and reliance

Each cross-boundary use binds the actual selected sources and material execution
basis, including uncommitted bytes where relevant. A moving selection identifies
how advancement is detected and which reliance must be reassessed. Git is one
possible carrier, not a mandatory identity system.

Changes and new counterexamples propagate through material assertion, execution
and evidence-use dependencies under [FOUNDATIONS Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse). Historical
evidence remains about its original subject. Reuse on a changed subject needs an
established applicability or preservation relation; rereading alone does not
establish it. A new release does not invalidate a still-selected older release,
and a changed hash alone establishes neither semantic incompatibility nor
continued validity. Unknown impact holds the dependent assurance or widens
assessment; it does not require unrelated work to restart.

text:
# RELEASE

Tier 2. Owns release publication: the release-publication bounded
context, release identities, project-qualified refs and the project
subtree, historical ref conservation, the three phases with candidate
construction, immutable RC or stable publication, exact-cut qualification and
monotonic version-line advancement, the selector and its relation to
consumer adoption, naming, release-scoped assets and the Product subject,
coordinated release-matched asset cohorts, acceptance, external
qualification dependencies and successor baseline conservation
(STDO-UP-015) with its disposition values. Its family table (F15) is §1
Foundation to law. It consumes [FOUNDATIONS](FOUNDATIONS.md) (§2 the
product lineage objects, among them the release objects candidate source,
release cut, release subject and version-line selector, defined there
once; §4 [Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), the core result algebra, and
[Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)),
[ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects) (the result of an intended
effect), [IDENTITY](IDENTITY.md) (object identity and its boundary with release
version), [EVALUATION](EVALUATION.md) (§1 claims, §5 acceptance),
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §7](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#7-layers) (AC-020, layer
and release separation) and [§8](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#8-calculus-identity)
(the calculus identity record issued at a release),
[SPEC_METHOD §6](SPEC_METHOD.md#6-lineage-and-release) (lineage and the
release version boundary) and
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#4-shared-installed-release-basis-and-toolchain-manager)
(the installed release basis, the adoption plan and the toolchain manager);
it defines none of those twice. Git, tag, branch, the `stdo://` URI forms
and the Product names of the Specification Stack are this Product's
realisation and toolchain terms. Every clause names the principle that
requires it (P0 to P6, FOUNDATIONS §3).

heading: RELEASE/1. Context and position
text:
## 1. Context and position

This member owns the release-publication bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:release-publication` under the selected complete
STDO basis. It owns the identities and transitions used to qualify,
publish and select released cuts. It does not own Product meaning or
consumer adoption; the consumer side of adoption is PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4
(P6, P3).

Release process is distinct from live project specification. Live
specification defines the current constitutional truth of the project.
Release process defines how one published point-in-time cut is evaluated,
bounded, named, published and made discoverable (P3).

The release authority selects one of two disjoint cut profiles (P3, P6):

- RC: product-local `v<version>-rc.<n>`, with a mutable `v<version>`
  version-line selector naming the greatest published positive RC ordinal;
- stable-v1: product-local `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`, with no RC suffix and
  no separate mutable selector at that ref, under
  [§2 Stable cuts](#stable-cuts).

Both profiles identify immutable published releases. The RC suffix does not
make a published release provisional or require a second final cut. The
stable profile is an explicit naming and discovery choice, not stronger
semantic qualification. Equal product-local names do not collapse different
Products. A mutable RC selector remains discovery, never an exact
constitutional, dependency, evidence or replay basis (P3, P6).

Release handling is downstream of intake triage. A bug, feature,
regression or release blocker first receives its change class, lawful
re-entry point, affected scope, downstream proof obligations and
version-line disposition
([SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#universal-intake-triage)). The existence
of an RC window does not authorise untriaged mutation (P0, P6).

Results. This member defines no result values of its own. Where it says
that an operation is refused, stops or fails closed, the operation does
not complete; its intended effect, with any part of it that began, is
reported under [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects), never as
`completed`.
Where it calls a release state invalid or a cohort incomplete, or says
that a verification fails, the condition named is a counterexample to the
predicate that check evaluates, and the check returns its value under
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). What the disposition
values of §9 are, §9 states. Purpose and material relation: release
outcomes combine with every other result in the one core, so a refused
publication or a failed verification is never read as a published or
qualified cut (P5, P6).

heading: RELEASE/2. Release identities
text:
## 2. Release identities

The release-publication context distinguishes (P3):

- Project Release Namespace: a stable repository-local key assigned by
  the Product release authority to one independently released source
  project;
- Project Subtree: the exact repository-relative source-project root and
  Git tree object selected for one cut;
- Candidate Source: the candidate source of FOUNDATIONS §2, the mutable
  source-project state constructing a possible successor;
- RC Branch: a mutable project-qualified carrier for the current
  candidate window;
- Immutable Release Cut: an annotated project-qualified Git tag plus its
  exact Product release subject (FOUNDATIONS §2), under the selected RC or
  stable profile; publication, qualification and acceptance retain their
  respective meanings; it realises the release cut;
- Version-Line Selector: the mutable project-qualified tag alias naming
  the highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut for that project and
  version line; it realises the version-line selector of FOUNDATIONS §2;
  and
- Release Branch: an optional mutable project-qualified convenience
  carrier aligned to the same latest-published commit as the selector.

Equal version text does not collapse these identities. Branches and the
version-line selector may move. An immutable release tag never moves (P3).

heading: RELEASE/2. Release identities/Project-qualified Git refs
text:
### Project-qualified Git refs

`<project>` is one explicit Project Release Namespace. It matches
`[a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*`, contains no slash, is unique within the
release source, and remains stable for the continuing release line. It is
assigned by the Product release authority. A directory name, display name,
definition label, package name or matching version cannot infer or
reassign it (P3, P6).

A shared release source uses these exact ref shapes for an RC-profile
publication (P3):

```text
RC branch:              refs/heads/rc/<project>/<version>
immutable RC cut tag:   refs/tags/<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>
version-line selector:  refs/tags/<project>/v<version>
release branch:         refs/heads/release/<project>/<version>
```

The short Git tag names are therefore `<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>` and
`<project>/v<version>`. A shared release source does not publish a future
cut or selector under the unqualified `v<version>-rc.<n>` or `v<version>`
refs (P3).

A single-project release source may retain the unqualified ref profile
only while it has exactly one independently released project and its
release record declares that profile. Adding a second independently
released project requires project-qualified refs before either project
publishes another cut (P3).

For the Specification Stack shared source, the allocated namespaces are
`specification_methodology`, `axiom_indexer` and `stdo_representation`.
These keys distinguish release refs; they do not merge the three Products
or imply a dependency or composition relation (P3, P6).

heading: RELEASE/2. Release identities/Stable cuts
text:
### Stable cuts

The `stable-v1` profile publishes an immutable release directly as
`refs/tags/<project>/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`. Each numeric component is a
nonnegative decimal integer, with no leading zero except the single digit
`0`. The tag is annotated, targets a commit and contains exactly one
standalone annotation line (P3):

```text
STDO-Release-Profile: stable-v1
```

Its exact release declaration names the same stable cut, declared payload,
source selection and predecessor. The installed manifest records
`release.profile = "stable-v1"` alongside the complete identity of
[Project-subtree release identity](#project-subtree-release-identity).
An RC manifest retains its prior shape; adding stable support must not
change the canonical bytes of a historical release manifest (P3, P4b).

The stable coordinate is available only on a fresh version line with no
same-version RC tag in either the historical or project-qualified namespace
and no historical unqualified bare-version tag. The stable tag itself is
create-only. A same-line collision or a missing, duplicated or different
profile marker refuses stable acquisition; bare spelling or annotation alone
cannot turn an RC selector into an immutable cut (P3, P5).

There is no separate version-line selector or RC branch for this profile.
A channel `stdo://channels/<major>.<minor>.<patch>` may discover that exact
immutable stable tag; its cut ordinal is absent (`null`), and resolution
must verify the stable profile and complete identity. That channel route
creates neither another tag nor mutable alias semantics. Consumer adoption
still follows §4 (P3, P6).

A published stable tag never moves. Any change to its qualifying bytes
requires a new version and a new immutable cut, not an RC added to the
already stable line. Historical RC lines keep their selector semantics,
refs, objects, peels and URIs; this profile neither finalises nor renames
them. An RC-labelled published release remains a proper release (P3, P4b).

heading: RELEASE/2. Release identities/Project-subtree release identity
text:
### Project-subtree release identity

In a shared release source, an immutable cut binds all of (P3):

- the Project Release Namespace and owning Product authority;
- the exact qualified Git ref and annotated tag object;
- the peeled commit and repository-root tree;
- the normalised repository-relative Project Subtree root at that commit;
- the Git tree object at that exact Project Subtree root;
- the declared Product member inventory and release-scoped claim bytes;
  and
- the predecessor and successor dispositions required by §9.

The Project Subtree root is a locator inside the exact peeled commit, not
Product identity. Its canonical spelling is the slash-separated Git path
from the repository root, with no leading or trailing slash and no empty,
`.` or `..` component; `.` alone denotes the repository root. Each
non-root component names the exact tree entry bytes traversed at that
commit. Moving a source project changes this locator and its cut identity
without reassigning the Project Release Namespace. If the source project
occupies the repository root, its project-subtree tree equals the
repository-root tree (P3).

A tag over a monorepo commit does not make sibling subtrees Product
members. Unrelated sibling bytes remain carrier state outside the declared
Product subject. Conversely, a member inventory or payload digest without
the qualified ref, commit, Project Subtree root and Project Subtree tree is
not a complete reacquirable release identity (P3, P6).

heading: RELEASE/2. Release identities/Historical ref and public-URI conservation
text:
### Historical ref and public-URI conservation

Project qualification is prospective. Existing unqualified refs retain
their names, objects, peels and public links. A historical tag object may
remain reachable through an additional archival ref, but it is not
recreated, re-annotated, moved or replaced. An immutable historical tag
remains the same object regardless of which preserving ref reaches it
(P3, P4b).

Product-local cut names and public logical release URIs also remain
unchanged. An RC logical STDO release remains
`stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/`; a stable release uses
`stdo://releases/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>/`. The project-qualified Git ref is
transport identity and is not inserted into that URI. Resolution binds
the public logical cut to its exact historical or project-qualified Git
ref and fails closed if one project-local coordinate names different tag
objects (P3, P5).

When one version line spans the transition, latest means the greatest
positive RC ordinal across that project's preserved historical cuts and
its qualified future cuts. The first qualified publication creates the
qualified selector. The historical unqualified selector is preserved at
its existing object and ceases to be the current selector for the shared
source; it is not force-moved to imitate the qualified namespace (P3).

heading: RELEASE/3. Phases
text:
## 3. Phases

The release process has three phases (P0, P3, P6):

1. mutable candidate construction;
2. immutable publication under the selected profile, with RC selector
   advancement only for an RC line; and
3. exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption.

An accepted RC needs no second final cut. RC publication immediately makes
the new highest ordinal discoverable through its selector. Stable publication
makes its one exact tag discoverable under the stable profile. Acceptance is
a verdict over the exact immutable subject, not a second carrier. A change
to qualifying bytes requires a higher RC on an applicable RC line or a new
version after a stable cut (P3, P6).

heading: RELEASE/3. Phases/Mutable candidate construction
text:
### Mutable candidate construction

During candidate construction (P0, P6):

- bounded fixes are allowed after intake triage;
- qualification and operator review may continue;
- release notes may remain draft until publication;
- the candidate branch may move; and
- mutable source is explicitly non-operative for released consumers.

The intended Product boundary, release-scoped claims, excluded
source-project state and qualification basis become explicit before
publication. A material scope change is repriced instead of being silently
absorbed (P2, P6).

heading: RELEASE/3. Phases/Immutable RC publication
text:
### Immutable RC publication

A published RC cut exists to provide one exact subject for review, replay
and possible acceptance. To publish it, the project (P3, P5, P6):

1. confirms the triaged scope and lawful constitutional re-entry;
2. declares the exact Product release subject and release-scoped claim
   set;
3. reconciles the release note and other release-facing assets to that
   subject;
4. runs the proportionate pre-RC qualification and operator checks;
5. commits the exact carrier;
6. resolves and records the exact Project Release Namespace, Project
   Subtree root and Project Subtree tree;
7. creates one annotated immutable `<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>` tag and
   an annotated `<project>/v<version>` selector tag over that same commit
   in a shared release source;
8. atomically pushes the carrier, RC branch, immutable RC tag, selector
   and optional release branch where the transport supports it;
9. verifies remotely that the immutable tag, selector and release branch
   resolve to the highest published RC commit; and
10. records enough ref, subtree, identity and inventory evidence to
    reacquire the cut without trusting a mutable checkout.

Each published RC tag is immutable. Further work increments `<n>` on the
same version line when the intended line remains applicable. It does not
require a minor-version increment merely because review found a bounded
repair. A published higher RC without matching selector advancement is an
invalid, fail-closed release state; it never authorises resolution of the
older cut as the version-line latest (P3, P5).

heading: RELEASE/3. Phases/Immutable stable publication
text:
### Immutable stable publication

Stable publication applies the same scope, source reconciliation, proportionate
checks, exact carrier, subtree and inventory obligations as RC publication.
It instead creates one stable-v1 annotated tag and any explicitly selected
release branch, with no RC branch or separate selector. Before publication,
verify the fresh-line conditions of [Stable cuts](#stable-cuts), bind remote
absence for the immutable tag and bind every mutable destination's expected
object. Publish the selected refs atomically where supported; a changed
expectation stops publication for reconciliation. Read back the remote tag
object, commit, subtree and declared assets. The release is publicly classified
as a normal published release; release-host flags do not replace exact identity
or qualification evidence (P3, P5, P6).

heading: RELEASE/3. Phases/Monotonic version-line advancement
text:
### Monotonic version-line advancement

On an RC-profile line, version-line advancement makes the newly published highest RC for one
Project Release Namespace discoverable (P3, P5):

1. identify the exact new immutable RC tag, ordinal and peeled commit;
2. confirm that no higher RC ordinal already exists on that line;
3. confirm the project-qualified selector is absent or currently resolves
   to a lower RC ordinal on the same project line;
4. atomically create or force-update the annotated `<project>/v<version>`
   selector to the new highest RC commit;
5. create or update `release/<project>/<version>` to the same commit when
   that optional carrier is used;
6. push the carrier, RC branch, immutable RC tag, selector and optional
   release branch atomically where the transport supports it; and
7. verify remotely that the selector peels to the highest RC commit and
   that the matching immutable annotated RC tag exists.

Advancement is refused when the target has no matching immutable annotated
RC tag, any higher ordinal already exists, the selector would move to a
lower RC, or the selector and release branch would not align to the same
highest commit (P5).

Forward movement is strictly monotonic by RC ordinal. A later defect is
repaired through a higher immutable RC, not by moving an old RC tag or
rolling the selector backward. The selector is therefore equivalent to
`v<version>-rc.latest`, while every concrete RC tag remains addressable
(P3).

heading: RELEASE/4. Selector and consumer adoption
text:
## 4. Selector and consumer adoption

An RC-profile version-line selector answers only (P6, P3):

> Which highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut currently exists on
> this version line?

It never answers:

> Which exact STDO cut governs this consumer?

A Product Definition may retain `stdo://channels/<version>` as its
discovery selector, but its operative basis is the exact
`stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/` or stable
`stdo://releases/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>/` URI and installed-manifest digest,
the installed release basis of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4. Moving the Git
version-line selector does not update any consumer. Adoption is a separate
explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs,
verifies and pins the selected immutable cut. RC resolution requires an
annotated selector with a distinct peeled commit; absence of a peeled
selector ref fails closed and cannot be interpreted as a lightweight
selector whose tag object is its commit (P6, P3, P5).

For an RC line, channel resolution enumerates the published RC tags for the selected
Project Release Namespace, including preserved unqualified historical cuts
during a namespace transition, selects the greatest positive ordinal,
requires that cut and the current selector to be annotated tags peeling to
the same commit, and fails closed when the selector lags or points
elsewhere. Channel adoption also refuses a same-line target whose ordinal
is below the Product Definition's current exact basis. A consumer that
intentionally retains an older cut names that immutable RC URI and digest
explicitly and uses exact-basis operations such as `sync`; it does not
express that choice through the latest-version channel (P5, P6).

For a stable line, channel resolution returns its verified stable-v1 cut
without ordinal comparison or a separate selector. A legacy bare selector is
never admitted as a stable exact basis; an ambiguous profile is refused. The
same digest-bound adoption operation applies to either profile (P3, P5, P6).

Presentation and mutation are separate invocations. The read-only plan,
the Adoption Plan of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4, binds the current Product
Definition bytes and basis to the target immutable cut, annotated tag
object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest, then emits a
deterministic plan digest. Mutation requires that exact digest as the
operator's acceptance and re-derives it before changing any Product
Definition. Selector, target, manifest or definition drift invalidates the
acceptance. A fleet uses the same law with one aggregate digest over all
exact per-definition plans. Planning inside a mutating invocation is not
external presentation and cannot authorise itself. The plan's hashing rule
and the manager's command boundaries are PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4 (P6, P3).

This split lets operators refer to `v<version>` for the latest published
RC without repeatedly incrementing the version line, while every governed
project retains reproducible exact-cut authority and changes only through
explicit adoption (P2, P3, P6).

heading: RELEASE/5. Naming
text:
## 5. Naming

The shared-source RC-profile naming shape is (P3):

- RC branch: `rc/<project>/<version>`;
- immutable RC tag: `<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>`;
- optional release branch: `release/<project>/<version>`; and
- mutable version-line selector tag: `<project>/v<version>`.

For example, on an RC line:

- candidate branch: `rc/example/3.0.0`;
- first immutable cut: `example/v3.0.0-rc.1`;
- second immutable cut: `example/v3.0.0-rc.2`;
- latest-release branch: `release/example/3.0.0`; and
- latest-published selector: `example/v3.0.0`.

A stable example is `example/v3.0.2`, with the stable-v1 marker and no
separate selector. The published tag is immutable.

The unqualified RC profile remains lawful only under the single-project and
historical-conservation conditions of §2. Projects may choose another
spelling only in a release source whose ref policy proves collision
freedom and preserves the same project namespace, mutable carrier,
immutable cut and mutable selector distinctions (P3).

heading: RELEASE/6. Release-scoped assets and the Product subject
text: ## 6. Release-scoped assets and the Product subject

heading: RELEASE/6. Release-scoped assets and the Product subject/Release-scoped assets
text:
### Release-scoped assets

An immutable release cut may carry release-scoped surfaces such as (P3, P6):

- release notes;
- release and installed-distribution manifests;
- dependency declarations;
- package or installed-carrier metadata;
- qualification receipts; and
- branch and tag identity declarations.

Before publication, each used surface is reconciled to the exact cut
subject. After publication, changing one of those bytes requires the
applicable immutable successor: a higher RC or a new version after stable. The
version-line selector has no content-reconciliation phase because it adds
no new Product bytes (P3).

Exact version and cut identity belong in release-scoped carriers and
consumer basis bindings (P3). How a live constitutional surface, Product
and requirements surfaces included, uses version labels is the
[SPEC_METHOD §2 Specification surface rule](SPEC_METHOD.md#specification-surface-rule).

heading: RELEASE/6. Release-scoped assets and the Product subject/Product subject and repository carrier
text:
### Product subject and repository carrier

Before qualification, the project declares (P3, P6):

- its Project Release Namespace and exact Project Subtree root;
- the exact Product member set or artifact constituting the release
  subject;
- the release-scoped claim surfaces describing that subject; and
- co-located mutable source-project fields excluded from both.

A repository commit carries those declared sets but does not make every
co-located file or sibling Project Subtree a Product member. The exact
Project Subtree tree and Product member inventory distinguish the subject
from the wider carrier. Once the immutable cut is published, no post-review
carrier delta is admitted into that cut. Publication-caused ticket or
source-work bookkeeping is recorded afterward on the continuing source
branch and cannot move the immutable cut tag (P3, P6).

heading: RELEASE/7. Coordinated release-matched asset cohorts/Source freeze and stable cohort construction
text:
### Source freeze and stable cohort construction

A declared stable cohort may select an exact `<major>.<minor>.<patch>` suffix
instead of the RC-profile suffix. Its contract names the complete required
Product and component set, current-source relationships and qualification
obligations. The historical RC-profile member set above does not limit an
explicitly selected successor cohort. Product identity and independent
third-party version pins remain distinct from the shared cohort version.

When a native package must include its derived documentation, tools or proof
views, construction first freezes the exact semantic source independently of
those generated bytes. The source record inventories every authoritative
member and native contract, classifies derived routes, and names all generated
exclusions with their owners. No authoritative source may be excluded merely
to make a digest agree. Derived candidates bind that source record, its exact
member digests and the intended cut URI. Generated frames remain projections
of their exact owners, not independent semantic authorities (P3, P5, P6).

All required installed assets are built and qualified before the native cut
is frozen. After its annotated tag and installed manifest exist, an external
cohort record binds the source freeze, complete native cut and every derived
Product subject without modifying embedded payload bytes. No asset must
embed its own containing manifest's digest. Source drift invalidates affected
derivations; generation may add only the declared auxiliary bytes. This
source-freeze construction preserves the same exact-subject, complete-ref,

heading: RELEASE/8. Acceptance/Acceptance criteria
text:
### Acceptance criteria

A release cut may be accepted when (P6, P3):

- proportionate prepublication qualification passed for the declared subject;
- independent exact-cut review passed where required;
- required operator review is complete;
- the intended release scope and successor relation are stable;
- release-scoped assets accurately describe the exact cut;
- all release-blocking gaps, including the findings that block promotion
  under [EVALUATION §5 When a finding blocks promotion](EVALUATION.md#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion),
  are closed or the claimed scope is explicitly narrowed; and
- the human Product authority accepted the exact immutable cut identity.

Each criterion is a mandatory gate in the sense of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse):
it applies irrespective of any selection of checks after a change, and
retained evidence satisfies it only under the validity conditions stated
there (P6).

Acceptance attaches to that immutable cut identity. It neither advances
nor rolls back the version-line selector. Consumer adoption separately
evaluates the exact latest target presented by the channel and mutates
only after its digest-bound plan is accepted (P6, P3; EVALUATION §5 is
the generic acceptance law).

heading: RELEASE/9. Successor baseline conservation (STDO-UP-015)/Deterministic-kind migration
text:
### Deterministic-kind migration

A successor that adopts the total deterministic kind of
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds)
preserves each existing evaluation operation's unchanged subject, admissible
reads, witness/log outputs, permitted writes, stops/results, authority and
invalidation conditions. That profile alone does not
establish the new kind's totality, closed dependencies or declared outcomes.
The old deterministic evaluation/proof definition supplies no general
termination argument. Assess each proposed use against this relation (P3, P6):

| Evidence and declared migration status | Successor disposition |
|---|---|
| Establishes the new totality, closed-dependency and outcome contract | Map to common F_D plus the unchanged operation profile and exact traversal binding. Preserve the evidence and grants. |
| New-kind eligibility is unestablished, and the owner has identified the missing evidence or a separately declared bounded successor and its remediation obligation | Keep that identified migration pending. The legacy operation retains only its lawful standing on its exact old basis while it remains applicable; it gains no successor F_D standing. A narrower domain or fuel-bounded implementation has its own contract, identity, exhaustion outcomes and affected preservation evidence; it does not retrospectively prove the old operation total or preserve every old continuation. |
| New-kind eligibility is unestablished and no supported remediation or successor classification has been selected | Retain the exact legacy meaning and evidence with an explicit unresolved successor-classification obligation until its owner disposes it. The legacy operation retains only its lawful standing on its exact old basis while applicable. Grant neither new F_D standing nor an automatic F_P label; the affected successor claim stays open. |

An old deterministic evaluator with unestablished termination or an
undeclared material dependency takes the second or third row, even if it
preserves the judged subject: the second row requires an identified evidence
gap/remediation or selected bounded successor; absent that, the third records
the unresolved classification. Evidence alone need not choose the owner's
remediation. This relation imposes no general decision procedure for totality.
These eligibility/remediation cases are not additional semantic dispositions
under this section. Generic role descriptions and schematic traversal contracts are not concrete
operations with an implementation to qualify; their use still binds the
kind and operation contracts when instantiated.

ODD admission and closure retain their named operation owners under
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5's authority boundary](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds).
Exhaustion
retains the evaluated predicate and its signature/traversal stop mapping,
as [the conformance examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish.

Immutable consumers keep their selected edition's meaning. New consumers
explicitly select the complete successor and operation profiles. A stable
concept URN is not its immutable calculus edition
([AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §8](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#8-calculus-identity)). Migration
records the old release, manifest, member and clauses and the applicable row
above. Current URN lookup never reinterprets history. A versioned import or
alias records its justified supersession and grants no broader permission.
Disposition and qualification retain the separate obligations of this
section; unresolved mappings block the affected successor claim.

Broadening operation purpose while strengthening totality, dependency and
evidence requirements is a substantive semantic change. A patch-shaped
version label by itself promises no compatibility. The release's version
assessment identifies the selected predecessor, affected consumer mappings
and remaining obligations. This relation settles no general version-line
policy and waives no acceptance gate.

heading: SPEC_METHOD/6. Lineage and release
text:
## 6. Lineage and release

Software is recursive and compositional. A released product may build the
next released version of itself, a dependent product, or downstream project
artifacts. The roles are distinct objects with distinct identities,
substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product,
install, artifact and product definition, defined once in FOUNDATIONS §2
(product lineage objects) with their governing rules and the compiler
analogy; the product definition is the source project's present-tense
surface, not the released artifact and not the builder that happens to be
running the build (P3).

The only exact operative release identifier is an immutable release-cut
tag under the selected [RELEASE profile](RELEASE.md#2-release-identities):
an RC cut or an explicit stable cut (P3). That cut is a
point-in-time release identity, a boundary over the feature set accepted
for that cut, and part of release metadata and release-process evaluation;
it is not part of the live project specification. On an RC line the mutable
`v<version>` tag is a discovery selector to the highest published ordinal; it is not an exact dependency, evidence or constitutional
basis and cannot silently change a consumer selection. How an active
constitutional surface uses version labels is the
[§2 Specification surface rule](#specification-surface-rule); shared
realisation surfaces should likewise describe current truth by role,
boundary and status rather than by release-line version labels. Release criteria, immutable
release-cut publication, selector advancement and the process for cutting a
release belong to [RELEASE §2 to §8](RELEASE.md#2-release-identities)
.

Successor baseline conservation is
[RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)
(P3, P6).

Layer and release separation holds
([AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §7](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-020-layer-and-release-separation)):
a calculus, its interpretation of a subject and its carrier encoding keep
independent content identities, judgments, supersession relations and
proof obligations, and none is automatically an independently released
product. One constitutional surface and its version boundary for a project
are
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §11](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#11-one-constitutional-surface-and-version-boundary).

text:
### Review findings and bug items

When findings from a review need a durable work carrier, record one linked bug
report for that review, with one entry per finding: stable identity, original
Reviewer severity and triage, exact subject/basis, violated claim, location and
chaseable evidence. Link it to the work item that issued the review. With no
findings, create no bug report. A sufficient existing direct-work carrier may
carry the same relations without a redundant ticket (P3, P2).

The Reviewer may record this report only when its activation grants the exact
artifact identity/path and effects. Otherwise it returns the findings and a
lawful Writer records them. Recording creates no repair, priority, admission or
closure authority. Keep the report within its evidence/read and visibility
restrictions: findings derived from a withheld capture are withheld from the
same recipients, including any report projection that reveals them. The
Product may bind a recognizable report naming pattern and exclusion route to
its actual access mechanism; a filename or separate lane alone enforces
nothing and grants no additional read (P6).

After Executive or other authorized decision-owner triage, the reviewed work
item carries a linked Bug items section. Each item records its identity,
original severity, assigned priority and reason, cause group, responsible owner,
source report/finding, disposition and state. The report remains the technical
finding source; the item is the decision and repair ledger. An actor/session
index, where used, points the Reviewer to its report and the triage/repair work
to the reviewed work item's ledger, rather than duplicating that truth (P3).

| Item state | Required trace |
|---|---|
| open | Finding and triage/disposition, with unresolved work named. |
| fixed | Exact repaired subject (commit or equivalent immutable identity) and repair evidence; not yet a claim of verification. |
| verified | The satisfied repair predicate and exact evidence; identify tests and, when required, the independent recheck/report. Tests alone are not labelled independent review. |

These are carrier states, not core evaluation results or acceptance. A required
recheck keeps its affected items unverified until the required result is
available and applicable. A test-verified fix needs no invented Reviewer when
the governing basis requires none; the optional Executive cadence is
[EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks).
Retained or deferred findings stay linked until their selected boundary, or
transfer with owner, disposition and destination when the work item closes.
Changing priority does not erase the original severity or the obligation (P6,
P4b).

# Deterministic contracts and sufficient observations

These self-contained finite examples apply
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](../AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds),
[FOUNDATIONS observation sufficiency](../FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation)
and [ACTIVATION results](../ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition).
They select no runtime or mandatory representation. Each fixture's finite
domain, policy and oracle below are its basis Γ. The companion
[Python program](deterministic_contracts.py) exhausts the computational
domains identified below using
only the standard library. Authority, witness-log permission and the
unperformed-assessment case are source-first logical-review cases, not
executable permission proofs. Run `python3 -I deterministic_contracts.py` in
this directory. A passing run supplies bounded model evidence; it is neither
independent review nor whole-method qualification.

heading: Deterministic contracts and sufficient observations/Operations and permissions
text:
## Operations and permissions

The examples' reads are their arguments, their model state is explicit, and
their only returned effects are values. Their functions read no clock,
filesystem or mutable global state. The executable harness prints a report;
that reporting effect is outside the modeled functions. The finite bounds
below prove termination independently of observing a successful run.

| Exact traversal | Domain, permission and termination | Complete oracle |
|---|---|---|
| `v_double` | `n∈{0,1,2}`; construction-only grant; one multiplication | Return respectively `{n:0,double:0}`, `{n:1,double:2}`, `{n:2,double:4}`. The value's availability grants no assessment, admission or closure. |
| `v_sorted_full` | Lists of length at most three over `{0,1,2}`; unchanged-subject evaluation; at most two adjacent comparisons | Satisfied iff all adjacent pairs are nondecreasing. Otherwise falsified with the first inversion `{index,left,right}`. `[2,1]` gives `{index:0,left:2,right:1}`. Return a separate witness; an optional witness-log grant may persist it without changing the subject. |
| `v_put_A` | Explicit modeled state `absent/A/B` and grant `allow/deny`; one table lookup | The six cells below specify the returned next state and request/refusal. No physical write is executed. |

| Input state | Allow: next state / decision | Deny: next state / decision |
|---|---|---|
| absent | A / request put_A | absent / refusal |
| A | A / request put_A | A / refusal |
| B | A / request put_A | B / refusal |

The request is a modeled effect proposal, not physical completion. A
denial's evaluated predicate is “this request is authorized”; the table and
code's `refusal` denotes the cause-qualified `permission_denied` signature
stop, which maps to falsified. Unknown physical
completion belongs to the actual effect owner's contract. Likewise, under
a construction-only grant, `v_double(2)` establishes candidate availability
only; a separate judgment, admission or closure claim has no supporting
operation or evidence.

Negative evaluation case: sorting `[2,1]` in place and then calling it an
assessment of the original violates the unchanged-subject profile. The
changed list may be a construction output under a construction grant; its
sortedness is not the original list's sortedness. The executable shows the
mutation and opposite original/successor sortedness results; logical review
applies the evaluation profile to reject the false attribution. Manual
evaluation and mixed human/software witness logging have the same permission
boundary. The script does not implement an authorization or log-admission
mechanism, so it makes no executable claim about that boundary.

heading: Deterministic contracts and sufficient observations/Exhaustion
text:
## Exhaustion

`v_copy` accepts lists of length at most two over `{0,1}` and fuel in
`{0,1,2}`. It copies one element per fuel unit; only a complete copy is its
candidate. It terminates after at most two copies. `v_sorted` accepts lists
of length at most three over `{0,1}` and the same fuel. It inspects one
adjacent pair per fuel unit, stopping at the first inversion, when every
pair has been checked, or when fuel ends. It terminates after at most two
comparisons. Its one declared outcome is a closed assessment report containing
the exact input/basis, inspected-pair evidence and any residual; such a
report can carry the `assessment_exhausted` stop with its indeterminate
result. The stop/report is one declared outcome; its availability to an
enclosing step is assessed separately.

| Selected application and observation | Assessed predicate and result | Work result | Signature and traversal stop |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v_copy([0,1],1)` retains prefix `[0]`, with no complete candidate | Complete copy is available: falsified | `incomplete` → falsified for output availability | `copy_exhausted` maps to falsified, cause fuel ended before the required output |
| `v_sorted([0,1,0],1)` inspects `(0,1)`, with the second pair unexamined | Whole list is sorted: indeterminate on admitted inspected-pair evidence | `candidate_ready` → satisfied for the closed report and transition evidence being available only | `assessment_exhausted` maps to indeterminate, cause performed assessment has insufficient evidence |
| An activated assessing step spends its budget in setup and never invokes `v_sorted` | No assessment result | `incomplete` → falsified for the step's own output availability; the unperformed assessment remains residual work | No traversal application exists and therefore no `v_sorted` judgment or stop exists; the enclosing step retains its own stop and cause |

The two declared exhaustion stops have different predicates and parent core
values. Neither maps to satisfied. A report's availability and its assessed
predicate are not one judgment. Lists of length zero or one are sorted
without inspecting a pair. An observed inversion falsifies sortedness even
when later pairs remain unexamined. No result is inferred from a planned
invocation. These are distinct bounded traversals, not totality proofs for
an unbounded operation. The setup-before-invocation row is a logical-review
case under ACTIVATION §3, not a result of the executable example.

heading: Deterministic contracts and sufficient observations/Continuation-sensitive sufficiency
text:
## Continuation-sensitive sufficiency

Fix one subject and the one-assessment policy Γ. States are `U` (unassessed),
`S` (satisfied report), `F` (falsified report) and `I` (indeterminate report).
Inputs are `assess_S`, `assess_F`, `assess_I` and `advance`. From U an assess
input records that report; from any assessed state it is refused as already
assessed, preserving state. `advance` preserves state and is allowed only
from S; it returns `block_unassessed`, `block_falsified` or
`block_indeterminate` from the other states. This is the complete transition
and decision rule for every state/input pair. There is no reset input in Γ.
A different contract can permit reassessment or re-entry.

The weak observation “satisfied assessment exists” maps U, F and I to false
and S to true. U and I nevertheless require incompatible first-assessment
decisions. Thus no decision function over that observation can preserve the
fixed policy. In a human handover, “not approved” similarly fails to say
whether to perform the first assessment or preserve a completed undecidable
assessment and follow its declared continuation.

Define `alpha(U)=(subject,basis,null)` and
`alpha(s)=(subject,basis,s)` for s in `{S,F,I}`, with those subject and basis
fixed by Γ. Define `delta_hat` and `T_hat` by the complete rule above on
these records. Every state/input satisfies
`delta=delta_hat o alpha` (with the unchanged input supplied) and
`alpha(T(s,u))=T_hat(alpha(s),u)`. The readouts “satisfied exists”, exact
standing, permitted first assessment and advance decision are preserved.
The program checks all 16 one-step cells and every length-four input
sequence from every state. Exact one-step preservation with the closed
domain and identical next-state basis also composes by induction to every
finite sequence in this model. Approximate models have no such automatic
bound.

All four states remain distinguishable. This is a sufficiency witness with
no state aggregation, not evidence of compression, minimum context,
cross-task context selection, Markov sufficiency outside Γ, or cheaper
operation. Authority and hold distinctions are exact in this example.

heading: Deterministic contracts and sufficient observations/Qualified references
text:
## Qualified references

For this fixture a complete assessed record carries subject, basis,
standing, producer, obligation/version, authority and invalidators. Exact
local keys `report:S`, `report:F`, `report:I` resolve those records. An
independent copy preserves all required fields and the preceding policy
readout. The pointer `candidate-v1` alone maps every report to the same
bytes/identity; S and I then require different continuations, falsifying
its sufficiency for that consumer. Adding a type name alone cannot repair
missing standing.

The acquisition model takes three report keys and the explicit booleans
accessible, target-present and basis-current. Its complete eight-row oracle
per key is: all four inaccessible cases return `inaccessible`; of the four
accessible cases, both absent-target cases return `missing`, the present but
old-basis case returns `stale`, and only the present/current case returns the
qualified record as `resolved`. This yields 24 tested cells. Unavailable,
missing and stale targets yield no usable record and keep the dependent
sufficiency claim unsupported; their actual gap, invalidation, refusal or
residual follows the consuming operation's owner, not a universal result
mapping added by this fixture. The executable also checks that resolution
does not mutate the record store and that valid readouts survive.

These access flags and version comparisons model an acquisition boundary;
they are not observed filesystem, transport or human-handover behavior.
The currentness test covers the declared basis-version invalidator only.
Other material invalidators require their own scoped evidence. Logical review
checks the human handover and required residual meanings; actual use remains
unperformed. A hash-based realization would additionally state its collision,
authenticity and access assumptions; no digest alone proves semantic
sufficiency. A manual document reference and a mixed handover can use the
same record and policy without any annotation architecture or event log.

heading: Deterministic contracts and sufficient observations/Finite maps and consumer adequacy
text:
## Finite maps and consumer adequacy

Fix the same subject/basis and reports `X={S,F,I}`. Qualified records are
`H={hS,hF,hI}` and views `V={vS,vF,vI}`. Policy readouts are
`D={advance,block_falsified,block_indeterminate}`. The complete functions are:

| X | `build:X→H` | `view:H→V` | Both `j:H→D` and `h:V→D` read out |
|---|---|---|---|
| S | hS | vS | advance |
| F | hF | vF | block_falsified |
| I | hI | vI | block_indeterminate |

The three rows prove pointwise `j=h o view`. Arrow equality here is pointwise
finite-function equality; composition is ordinary composition and identities
return their inputs. The constant subject-only projection cannot factor j:
hS and hI share its output but require different readouts.

The following is a finite mathematical argument and executable structural
check, not a qualified categorical demonstration under FOUNDATIONS.
For the structural counterexample, take the finite chain category with
objects X,H,V,D and exactly the displayed generated function for each ordered
pair in that chain, including all identities and composites. There are ten
arrows; equality compares their endpoints and pointwise action. The target
terminal category has object `*` and only `id_*`. Send every source object
to `*` and every arrow to `id_*`: identities and composition are preserved,
yet that map cannot recover j's distinct readouts. The program exhausts
identity and associative composition checks for this bound fragment and
the terminal map. Those structural checks and the explicit counterexample
support their finite claims, not consumer adequacy of an arbitrary functor.
The full categorical demonstration still requires the applicable a_c
representation and supporting assessment under FOUNDATIONS; these executable
tables do not replace those obligations or discharge unresolved H1.

heading: Deterministic contracts and sufficient observations/Migration and comparison
text:
## Migration and comparison

The five declared traversals `v_double`, `v_sorted_full`, `v_put_A`,
`v_copy` and `v_sorted` have explicit closed dependencies, bounded operation
arguments and declared outcomes. Their finite proofs establish the eligibility
conditions of RELEASE's first row within their exact domains and profiles;
this is author evidence, not independent acceptance. The transition and
reference-acquisition functions are finite mathematical fixtures, not additional
adopted a_c operations. An old evaluator with an undeclared clock dependency or missing
termination evidence fails new-kind qualification despite preserving its
subject. It takes the pending-evidence or unresolved row of
[RELEASE's migration relation](../RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration),
retaining its exact old edition. A future fuel-bounded repair has a distinct
traversal and exhaustion meaning. A kind never grants broader writes.

An optional representation experiment can compare the complete plain-text
record, an equivalent qualified reference, and the insufficient candidate
pointer. Vary retained, absent and stale counterexamples separately, hold
substantive information/access fixed when claiming representation benefit,
and count acquisition, rendering, reasoning, repair and assurance costs at
declared boundaries. The finite examples above test correctness; they supply
no measured architecture or retention benefit.
